# Persist faff run state across machines

## WHY
A beep-boop run started on one host should be resumable on another. Today `.faff/runs/` is repo-local, so a run is pinned to the machine that started it.

## WHAT
Make an in-flight run's ledger + per-issue artifacts resumable from a second machine that has the same repo checked out.

## HOW
Unclear. The artifacts live under `.faff/` which is gitignored, so they don't travel with the repo. Options span: (a) commit a subset of run state to a dedicated branch; (b) push run state to the tracker as structured comments; (c) an external object store keyed by run-id. Each has different durability, contention, and privacy characteristics, and the concurrency model for two machines touching one run is undefined — does the second machine take over, or run alongside? The worktree-registry seam (FAFF-82) is also machine-local and would need rethinking. Significant architectural uncertainty; this may need splitting into a design spike first.

## DONE
- [ ] a run can resume on a second machine (mechanism TBD)

Mechanism undecided across three very different architectures; concurrency semantics undefined; likely needs splitting.
